mainEntity.name: Is a CPA better than a regular accountant?

acceptedAnswer.text: A CPA has met additional education, experience, and ethical standards. For complex work like audit, restructuring, or board-level reporting, a CPA designation can be required or strongly preferred. For routine tax returns and BAS, a registered tax agent who is not a CPA may be equally suitable. Our matching finds the right credential for your specific need.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my situation actually requires a CPA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most personal and small-business tax needs — individual returns, BAS, bookkeeping, and routine GST — do not require a CPA; a registered tax agent is qualified to handle them. A CPA becomes relevant for assurance and audit work, complex multi-entity restructuring, not-for-profit governance, or when a regulator, board, or contract specifically calls for a CPA-signed report. If you are unsure, tell us what you need in the questionnaire and we will match you with the right level of qualification.

CPA fees reflect the additional qualifications and the complexity of the work they typically handle. For specialist audit or structuring, a CPA is the right investment. For straightforward compliance, a non-CPA registered agent may be more cost-effective. We match based on what you actually need so you do not overpay for credentials you will not use.

mainEntity.name: How quickly will a matched CPA contact me?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most matches are completed within 60 seconds of finishing the questionnaire. Your matched CPA will typically reach out within 2 hours, or you can call for immediate assistance to discuss your needs.

mainEntity.name: Can a CPA help with not-for-profit or charity governance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The matched CPA advises on not-for-profit governance, ACNC compliance, and audit requirements — ensuring your charity or association meets its regulatory obligations and maintains its charitable status.

mainEntity.name: Can a CPA sign an audit report?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A CPA with the appropriate ASIC auditor registration can sign external audit reports. The matched firm confirms the right credential for your specific audit requirement — statutory, special-purpose, or grant compliance.

Yes. The matching service is free for individuals and businesses. We are engaged by the accounting firms in our network, not by you. You are under no obligation to proceed with any matched firm, and the matched CPA gives you a clear quote before any work begins.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a CPA, CA and IPA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Australia has three major professional bodies: CPA Australia (CPA), Chartered Accountants ANZ (CA), and the Institute of Public Accountants (IPA). All three require education, experience, and ethics commitments. Our network includes members of all three bodies — tell us if your situation requires a specific designation and we will match accordingly.

blocks.heading: CPA Accountant — what we can help with
blocks.text: SPECIALIST NETWORKCPA Accountant — what we can help withWhat makes a CPA different?A CPA has completed CPA Australia's postgraduate program, fulfilled supervised experience requirements, and commits to ongoing professional development and a strict code of ethics. This matters when you need assurance work (audits), complex restructuring, or board-level reporting where a recognised credential carries weight. Not every accountant needs to be a CPA — but when you do, our matching ensures you are connected with one.When to specifically ask for a CPAYou might specifically need a CPA for: external audit and assurance engagements, reporting to a board or external stakeholders, complex multi-entity restructuring, not-for-profit or charity governance, or when a lender, regulator, or contract requires a CPA-signed report. In our questionnaire, tell us if you need a CPA specifically and we will narrow the match accordingly.CPA vs CA vs IPA — top-tier qualificationsAustralia has three major professional bodies: CPA Australia (CPA), Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CA ANZ), and the Institute of Public Accountants (IPA). All three require education, experience, and ethics commitments. It is worth noting that Chartered Accountants (CA ANZ) hold an equivalent top-tier professional designation to CPAs and carry identical legal standing for audit and tax advisory work — so a CA is just as highly qualified as a CPA for assurance, complex structuring, and strategic advice. Our network includes highly qualified members of all three bodies, and we match you with the credential that best fits your situation.
